review.interpretation: Every retained title describes a company-level financial, ownership, enforcement, financing, management or material-operation state. This is relevance precision, not predictive value or impact strength.

iterations.finding: The first 200-item sample retained about 14 percent procedural or attachment-only noise.
Procedural debt, governance, fund-occupancy and adviser attachments were removed; obvious sample mismatch fell to about 2.5 percent.
Three remaining procedural documents yielded about 98.5 percent observed precision.
The three remaining classes were excluded; their deterministic replacement rows had no obvious topic mismatch in the 111-task population.

A fresh 25-task acquisition batch exposed annual related-party estimates, rating reports, allocation results, adviser commitments and review-meeting arrangements; narrow procedural exclusions were added.
The expanded 136-task sample removed the final transaction-process representation class.

Fourteen additional tasks completed a clean 50-symbol checkpoint and exposed written confirmations, supervision reports, regulatory-letter replies, briefing notices, procedural rules and small-financing authorizations; these narrow classes were removed before the 200-title review was repeated.

known_boundaries: Title-only relevance cannot measure transaction size, severity or novelty.
Annual reports and recurring pledge events can duplicate information already present in core stock data; residualization and novelty weighting remain mandatory.
Independent human annotation remains pending for a formal production gate.
Historical ST and delisting status remains PIT-unverified and is not inferred from current names.
